basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et ait Dominus ad Abraham: Sara uxor tua pariet tibi filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Isaac.'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et ait Dominus ad Abraham: Sara uxor tua pariet tibi filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Isaac. Isaac interpretatur Risus, nec dubitandum est eum ita vocatum ab eo, quod, audita ejus nativitate, Abraham riserit in corde suo. Risus autem ille decenter significat gaudium Novi Testamenti, in quo filii promissionis, inhabitante in eis Domino, in aeternum exsultabunt.
